name: Opus Control
description: Transaction and position control: reconciling internal records against external statements, and working the breaks that reconciliation raises through to proof.
notes:
READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING IT IS A PLACEHOLDER.

This registration exists to test FR-20's central claim — 'adding a product is a registration exercise, not a platform code change' — which was previously unfalsifiable, because with one product there was nothing to be product-agnostic ABOUT. Adding this file required no change to any file under libs/ or server/, and that is the entire point of it.

Its `status` is `registered` rather than `active` because the demo tenant's catalog contains no Control data. That is the honest state and a deliberately chosen one: fabricating recon and settlement tables would make the registry look complete while proving nothing, and would put invented data in front of anyone demonstrating the platform. `groundingFor()` reports this product as ungrounded, product identification still recognises its vocabulary, and a prompt about breaks therefore gets 'Control's metadata is not in this tenant' rather than a fluent dashboard built out of EDM's securities — which is exactly the failure the whole product concept exists to prevent.

It registers no components, templates or System Pages for the same reason: there is nothing behind them here. What it does register is vocabulary, which costs nothing to be true.

glossary.definition: A discrepancy between two records that should agree — an internal position against a custodian statement, a ledger balance against a bank's. The unit of work in this product.
The test that decides whether two records are the same thing, including its tolerances. A break is what is left after every match rule has run.
The evidenced statement that two sets of records agree for a period, with every break either matched or explained. The output the whole reconciliation exists to produce.
An account held with another institution, and the classic subject of a cash reconciliation.
A break outstanding beyond its expected resolution window. Ageing is the primary risk signal in reconciliation, more so than count.

terminology.means: A discrepancy between two records that should agree, awaiting matching or explanation.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A service outage, or a page break. A break here is a unit of reconciliation work.

terminology.means: The pairing of two records that a match rule has determined represent the same item.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A string match or a search hit.

terminology.means: The evidenced agreement of two record sets for a period, with every break resolved or explained.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A mathematical proof, or a proof of concept.

terminology.means: A record that no match rule paired, and therefore a break awaiting investigation.
An account held with another institution, reconciled against that institution's statement.
The process of comparing two record sets under match rules and resolving what does not agree.

instructions: Ageing outranks volume: an aged break is a risk statement, a break count is a workload statement. A page about reconciliation health leads with ageing.
Never present a match rate without the population it is a rate of — 99% matched is meaningless without knowing whether the remainder is four items or four thousand.

hints.whenToUse: Any request about reconciling two record sets, the breaks that reconciliation raises, match rates, or evidencing agreement for a period.
exampleQuestions: Show me aged reconciliation breaks by custodian
Build a cash reconciliation proof dashboard for month end

capabilities.label: Read reconciliations
capabilities.description: Reconciliation runs, their match rules and their results.

capabilities.label: Sign off a proof
capabilities.description: Attest that a period reconciles. Held separately from resolving breaks, because the person who cleared the work should not be the person who certifies it.

roles.label: Reconciliation Operator
roles.description: Works breaks. Cannot sign off the proof they worked towards.
